title: Suspected drug boat erupts in fireball as US strike kills four
text:
By JACK TOLEDO

Published:  23:32 AEST, 20 September 2026   |  Updated:  23:32 AEST, 20 September 2026

458

View  comments

The US military has launched another lethal strike on a suspected drug trafficking vessel, killing at least four on board.

The strike, carried out Saturday under the authority of US Southern Command and Joint Task Force Southern Spear, targeted what was described as a suspected narco-terrorist boat in the Caribbean.

'Confirmed intelligence revealed the vessel's active involvement in narco-trafficking. The operation killed four narco-terrorists,' US Southern Command confirmed in a statement about the deadly encounter.

Operation Southern Spear has killed at least 231 people in 69 strikes since the Trump administration launched the operation in September 2025.

The controversial military campaign is aimed at disrupting drug trafficking across maritime routes.

Just days before, on Wednesday, another alleged narco-terrorist vessel was sunk after the ship was raided by American forces.

Officials said the boat was used as a refueling station for drug traffickers at sea linked to Los Choneros, a violent narco-terrorist organization.

The crew aboard the alleged narco-terrorist vessel was transferred to Ecuadorian authorities before it was obliterated.

US Southern Command and Joint Task Force Southern Spear launched a lethal strike on a suspected drug trafficking vessel, leaving four dead, on Saturday

Officials said the vessel was traveling along 'known narco-trafficking routes in the Caribbean

'Alongside our Ecuadorian partners, we are relentlessly pursuing narco-terrorists who prey on our citizens, undermine hemispheric security, and leave death and suffering in their wake. This deliberate, lawful, and precise operation saves lives and makes our citizens—from Ecuador to the United States—safer,' said Southern Command Commander Gen Francis Donovan.

The Department of Defense detailed how an official described Operation Southern Spear as largely successful in an update earlier this month.

According to the department, an official said President Donald Trump made a promise to 'take the fight to the cartels and narco-terrorists who have poisoned our communities for far too long.'

'Under Secretary [of War Pete] Hegseth, the Department of War is delivering on that promise and — in the Western Hemisphere specifically — the results are simply undeniable,' added an unnamed official.

Hegseth visited Panama last month, where he claimed that Colombia, Guatemala and Honduras agreed to authorize the US to operate missions against criminal groups in their countries, according to the Associated Press.

On Wednesday, another alleged narco-terrorist vessel was sunk after the ship was allegedly used as a refueling station for drug traffickers at sea

The boat was allegedly linked to Los Choneros, a violent narco-terrorist organization. Adolfo Macias, leader of the Los Choneros pictured on August 12, 2023, before he was extradited to the US in 2025

Guatemala denied that an agreement was ever reached. However, US forces began launching operations with Ecuador in March.

Critics have questioned whether there is enough evidence to conclusively link the targeted boats to drug trafficking operations.

The legality of the fatal strikes has also been challenged by military lawyers and legal experts.

However, the Trump administration has defended the legality of the killings.

The White House has said Trump 'determined' that the US is in an armed conflict with cartels and that the suspected drug-running boats were 'combatants,' according to The New York Times.

Hegseth previously said the mission 'defends our Homeland, removes narco-terrorists from our Hemisphere, and secures our Homeland from the drugs that are killing our people.'

Secretary of War Pete Hegseth visited Panama last month, where he claimed that Colombia, Guatemala and Honduras agreed to authorize the US to operate missions against criminal groups on their land. Guatemala denied that they had come to an agreement (Hegseth pictured on September 18 at a ceremony in remembrance of US military prisoners of war and those missing in action)

He added: 'The Western Hemisphere is America's neighborhood - and we will protect it.'

The Daily Mail has reached out to the Department of War for comment.
